NGBoost operates as a probabilistic extension of gradient boosting, where each iteration fits a distribution rather than a scalar mean. This is achieved through natural gradient descent, ensuring stability in probabilistic fitting. The core innovation lies in its ability to output full conditional distributions, enabling uncertainty quantification. In GSI, these distributions serve as Bayesian priors, which are then calibrated using conformal methods to ensure validity. In GSE, they enable dynamic state transitions from point forecasts to distributional predictions, supporting interval-based decision-making. The method's reliance on parametric families introduces vulnerability to model misspecification, necessitating post-hoc recalibration and walk-forward validation to maintain reliability.
